claims.text: The Grafana dashboard 'Đơn Hàng API' has panels 'Requests per second, by status code', '5xx responses per second' and 'p95 response time'; the p95 panel is histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))) over every endpoint.
An SLI is a measured ratio of good events to all valid events, such as the share of POST /api/v1/orders requests not answered with a 5xx (glossary; outline item 1).

UseHttpMetrics is the first middleware in the API pipeline, so later ones, including ExceptionHandlingMiddleware that turns an exception into a 500, run inside it; it counts every request except /metrics with its final status code and duration.

prometheus-net.AspNetCore's HTTP metrics: counter http_requests_received_total and histogram http_request_duration_seconds, labelled code, method and endpoint (the route template, e.g. api/v1/orders).
claims.source_hint: prometheus-net README, ASP.NET Core HTTP request metrics; docs/design/slo.md lines 8-10 @ stage-4

claims.text: A Prometheus histogram's _bucket series with label le counts every observation less than or equal to that bound (cumulative); the _count series counts all observations.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs, Metric types: Histogram; Histograms and summaries

claims.text: increase(v[range]) gives how much a counter grew over the range; it is extrapolated from the samples in the range and may return non-integer results even for counters.
Requests that fail before reaching the API, at Caddy (the lab's reverse proxy in front of api) or at the cluster's Gateway, are not counted by the SLIs.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/slo.md line 12; docker-compose.yml caddy service (line 215 comment); STAGE.md staging Gateway @ stage-4

claims.text: slo.md SLIs: S1 POST api/v1/orders and api/v2/orders not 5xx out of every POST to them; S2 same requests within bucket le="0.512"; S3 the two product GETs not 5xx, catalog-reads 503 bad; S4 POST refund within le="2.048".
2 seconds is not a bucket bound of http_request_duration_seconds; the nearest bounds are 1.024 and 2.048 (prometheus-net default buckets double from 0.001 s).
claims.source_hint: docs/design/slo.md lines 29-30 @ stage-4; prometheus-net source HttpRequestDurationMiddleware default buckets (ExponentialBuckets(0.001, 2, 16))

claims.text: S4 counts against 2.048, slightly looser than YC-7; an exact 2-second count needs its own bucket at 2 s, and stage-4 does not change the buckets.
YC-7: a customer's refund request is received and answered within 2 seconds, even when the payment gateway does not answer or fails.

slo.md: 429 from the per-customer orders limit and other 4xx are not bad (correct answers to a wrong or excessive request); 503 from catalog-reads is bad (a valid request refused for lack of room, seen as an error).

The orders policy is a fixed window of 10 orders per customer (1 minute in Program.cs, 10 s in the lab via RateLimiting__Orders__Window); refusals become 429. The catalog-reads concurrency limiter (20 running, 5 queued) refuses with 503.

slo-report.sh: promql sends one query to /api/v1/query and prints its value (0 if empty); sli queries round(sum(increase(...[1h]))) for good and total; awk prints the ratio, n/a when total is 0; report uses $orders for S1/S2, $products for S3, $refund for S4, as slo.md does.
claims.source_hint: scripts/backend/slo-report.sh lines 12-16, 27-42 @ stage-4; docs/design/slo.md lines 22-27, 45-55 @ stage-4

claims.text: The lab's Prometheus keeps no long history, so slo-report.sh reads a 1-hour window.

In a PromQL label matcher, =~ reads the value as a pattern (an RE2 regular expression, where braces are special) and = matches it exactly; the braces in $products are escaped because of the =~ matcher.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs, Querying basics: Time series selectors, label matchers; scripts/backend/slo-report.sh lines 28-29 @ stage-4

claims.text: histogram_quantile estimates a percentile from bucket counts, only as precisely as the bucket bounds allow; it does not count requests above a threshold.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs, Querying: Functions, histogram_quantile(); devops.l2.histograms-and-percentiles summary line 4

claims.text: CPU and memory measure how hard the process works, not whether answers were right or in time; they help find why after an SLI shows that service dropped.
When product reads far outnumber orders, slow orders hardly move a p95 computed over every endpoint together.
claims.source_hint: follows from claim 1 (sum by le over all endpoints) and claim 17

claims.text: Counting in front of the API (Caddy, Gateway) is worth its cost when failures there are a real share of what customers meet; slo.md does not use such metrics.
If a 429 limit is wrong for customers, change the limit rather than counting 429 as bad in S1.

slo-report.sh runs on the host with the lab started with COMPOSE_PROFILES=monitoring; it places 2 orders and product reads, reports, stops db while 4 orders get 500, starts db again, places 2 more (201) and reports again.
